Python 3 stdlib only; no network; no file writes; no import of the counter (LANE/.ufo/waves/round-93/c93_conditional.py) and no copy of any case input or fixture stem into the source (the counter's anti-table checks both). Work from the contract and the RFC text at LANE/.ufo/waves/round-93/L1/src/rfc9110.txt; do not read the counter's reference implementation to derive behaviour, and say in your report whether you did.

Also deliver a real `--selftest` mode in the same file: isolated in-memory fixtures that assert both exit codes (0 for a decision, 1 for a refusal) and stable finding ids for the failure it reports, runnable as `python3 -B LANE/scripts/conditional_eval.py --selftest`, exit 0 on pass.

and record the exact reading (candidate=absent is the expected base reading). Then prove the tool directly: copy your tool to /fast/scratch/hyaku/kake-r93/ExecC2Tool/cand.py, and run at least 12 inputs you derive from the contract yourself (six decisions, six refusals) as stdin/stdout transcripts in your receipt, plus `python3 -B LANE/scripts/conditional_eval.py --selftest`.
